ghats.name: Jampanna Vagu Main Bathing Ghats
ghats.description: Extensive concrete steps and stone ghats constructed along both banks of the stream. Features continuous water supply via overhead pipelines/showers (fed by Godavari lifting projects during low water periods), changing enclosures for women, high-power floodlighting, and permanent pedestrian bridges.

ghats.name: Kannepally & Surrounding Sub-Ghats
ghats.description: Secondary bathing stations situated closer to the Kannepally Saralamma shrine to handle peak crowd surges.

safety_rules: Strictly avoid crossing metal safety barricades and deep water zones.
No diving from bridges or elevated banks.
Do not drop plastic waste, soap, or synthetic shampoo bottles into the sacred stream.
Follow instructions from Expert Swimmers, NDRF/SDRF teams, and Police personnel stationed along the banks.
Keep children close and use designated shallow bathing zones.
significance: Jampanna Vagu is a sacred forest stream (tributary of Sampenga Vagu/Godavari River) named after Jampanna, the tribal warrior prince and son of Goddess Sammakka. He fought valiantly against Kakatiya forces and laid down his life in this stream. Tribal tradition attributes the stream's natural reddish tint to Jampanna's blood (geologically rich in red soil nutrients). Devotees perform Punya Snanams (holy dips) here to wash away sins, seek healing, and pay homage to tribal martyrs before offering prayers at the Gaddelu platform.
